doc.title: Dave Liebman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Open Sky, PM Records and Petter Wettre's Lighthouse solo transcriptions
summary: The WBAI Open Sky concert on Gene Perla's PM label, and a Norwegian student's book transcribing every Liebman and Grossman solo from Lighthouse.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: I’m going to skip over the Elvin dates, because we talked about that.
They have the order – is that the order – I asked you this – is that the order of recording?
It’s all – it’s totally chronological, from when the dates were recorded. Open Sky with Frank Tusa and Moses.
WBAI Free Music Store, live concert. That’s right. That’s the beginning of the trio, first music of “mine,” part of a collective.
PM Records was Gene Perla’s label, right?
First guy to start his own label. PM, it was a cooperative deal. We were in it together. It was that. It was what everybody does. Gene’s a very entrepreneurial guy.
He’s everything. He knows everything. Gene is the most well-rounded guy of all – we all know.
Just speaking of that, while we have him up for a moment, he put out a book of transcribed solos of you and Grossman from Elvin Jones at the Lighthouse.

Done by a Norwegian student of mine, a great saxophone player who did like eight bars a day for over a year, and did it, incredible, and then played the solos, played them, certainly Steve’s. Mine are a little – he played Steve’s solos. We did gigs. We played the solos. Petter Wettre, from Norway, from Oslo.
Yeah, it’s 100 pages, everything me and Steve played.
Has the book sold much, do you know?
People – not much, but it’s the kind of book that people, because of the variety of the record . . .
Talk about a niche market, right?

Nobody can play it. Nobody can get through 3 pages. It’s like when I called Grossman and talked to him, the first time I talked to him in like 30 years. I was in town, playing with Italian cats. He said, “Oh, Steve was just here.” I said, “You got his number?” “Yeah, call him, call him.” “Steve, by the way, somebody transcribed – it’s great.” “Is it right, Lieb?” I said, “I have no idea.” He said, “Okay. Let me see it.” That’s my last thing with him.
